summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney transplantation, type 1 diabetes, and recurrent multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections was admitted with fevers, chills, nausea, and malaise. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and elevated creatinine, likely due to infection and poor oral intake. Urine culture grew ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, sensitive to meropenem and ciprofloxacin. She was treated with intravenous meropenem and transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for a 10-day course. Renal ultrasound showed worsened resistive indices in the transplant kidney, but function improved with IV fluids and infection control. Cyclosporine dosing was adjusted, and valsartan was restarted. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, restart nitrofurantoin prophylaxis, monitor blood sugars, and follow up with transplant and urology for ongoing management.
problems: Acute kidney failure with tubular necrosis
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
